newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on South American crop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on South American crop.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on persistent reminders of near-ideal crop weather in South American soybean growing areas, traders said.
"Plantings are almost completed and the crop is off to a good start," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
The market was pressed early as values corrected after a jump early this week left the January contract drifting above a key chart level of $7.00 per bushel, traders said.
But the soybean market was underpinned by active U.S. exports of soybeans and soy products and a continued strong soybean crush pace in the U.S., sources said.

The National Oilseed Processors Association Thursday reported the U.S. soybean crush for the week ended December 18 at 30.594 million bushels, below the 30.732 million the previous week but sharply above the 27.177 million crushed the corresponding week a year ago.

Volume was thin and the market was in a holiday mode with roughly 10 commission houses and funds each featured sellers of about one-half million bushels each of the January and March contracts, traders said.
Soybeans closed three to 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with January down 5-3/4 at $7.02.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 40,000 contracts, below the 50,691 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Continental Grain bought 700 March $7.25 calls at 9-3/4 cents, Prudential Securities sold 300 January $7.00 calls at six to seven cents and Lind Waldock sold 300 July $7.00 calls at 32-1/4 to 32-3/4 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, below the 14,395 traded Thursday, the CBOT said.
